subject: Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Hi all,

I am currently implementing the generalized extreme value distribution in brms, which proved to be rather complicated.
Basically, I have to constrain the shape parameter xi to a certain interval based on other (predicted) model parameters to avoid
leaving the definition space of the response variable, which may cause many divergent transitions (the .stan file is attached).

These other predicted parameters are defined and computed in the model block, and not in transformed parameters,
to avoid that rstan is writing them to a csv-file in the temp folder even if not returned to the user later on
(at least this was rstan's behavior a few months ago when I moved most stuff to the model block).
These csv-files will get really big for huge models, which reportedly caused problems.

Long story short, I want to save the samples of the shape parameter xi, even though it depends on variables
defined in the model block. Or, I want to find a way to make sure that samples of quantities, which are never returned
to the user anyway, are not written to csv-files in the temp folder when defined in transformed parameters.

Many thanks for your help!

Best,
Paul

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Hi, my quick question (without having seen any of the models) is that you might want stronger priors.  Many times when a model is hard to fit, the problem is that the fitting algorithm is spending time in weird, remote areas of the posterior that correspond to data distributions which are not of any substantive interest.  Even a weak prior can be enough to make a big difference.
A

parts:
I have tried informative priors, but that doesn't stop Stan from leaving the definition space. The GEV distribution is defined on y values satisfying

1 + xi (y - mu) / sigma > 0

which kind of sucks since it depends on all three parameters of the distribution.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Hey Paul, one way to save xi would be to write a function that computes xi (and the intermediate stuff you need to eventually compute xi) and then use that function in the model block and then again in the generated quantities block, where you can create the xi that's actually saved. This will duplicate some computations but I'm not sure if there's a way around that at the moment (although maybe someone else will have a brilliant work-around). 

Jonah

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Definitely what Jonah said---recomputing in generated quantities
is very cheap because there are no derivatives and it's only
done once per iteration.

There's no way to get around that scaling by hand that you're
doing because we don't yet allow varying upper and lower bounds
on a variable (on our to-do list). You sidestepped the Jacobian
calc by putting the prior on the unconstrained form of xi. I
don't know if that makes sense in your generative model, but you
could put the prior directly on xi if you include the Jacobian
(which is described in the manual---we mean to expose those to
the language soon, too, for just this kind of application).

- Bob

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Paul,

I would fit towards the mean not towards the parameters of your distribution. Since the mean for GEV is not defined for zeta >= 1(shape)
maybe go for the mode instead. This doesn't change things for correctness point of view, but from sampling.

The inv_logit with max/min, doesn't feel good to me in MCMC. Did you try to constrain your parameters? So they get truncated.

Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
> On Feb 2, 2017, at 11:59 PM, andre.pfeuffer via Stan users mailing list <stan-...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
>
> Paul,
>
> I would fit towards the mean not towards the parameters of your distribution. Since the mean for GEV is not defined for zeta >= 1(shape)
> maybe go for the mode instead. This doesn't change things for correctness point of view, but from sampling.
>
> The inv_logit with max/min, doesn't feel good to me in MCMC. Did you try to constrain your parameters? So they get truncated.

Presumably the bad feeling is from the discontinuities
in min and max? That does seem like it could be a problem
in the constraining transform:

real scale_xi(real xi, vector y, vector mu, vector sigma) {
vector[2] bounds;
real lb;
real ub;
bounds[1] = - inv(min((y - mu) ./ sigma));
bounds[2] = - inv(max((y - mu) ./ sigma));
lb = min(bounds);
ub = max(bounds);
return inv_logit(xi) * (ub - lb) + lb;
}

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Saving samples of quantities computed based on variables defined in the model block
parts:
Suppose you have a 2-vector v and the function y = min(v).
Then the derivatives dy/dv[1] and dy/dv[2] are discontinuous
at the point where v[1] = v[2]. So you have to cross a discontinuity
in derivatives to move from (0.99, 1) to (1.01, 1). That can
be problematic. It's not that HMC will do the wrong thing, just
that it'll revert to a rejection sampler if it can't smoothly
cross boundaries; how bad that is will vary from problem to problem.

- Bob
